My absolute best advice for you, as someone who just rescued a 4 week old puppy (who is now almost four months)... with as many children and things to do as you do, do not get a puppy. Go to a shelter and adopt an older dog, or find a retired breeding female who has been tested for temperament time and time again.
You don't have time for the puppy stage, (the chewing, mouthing, sleepless nights, potty training it is truly, truly, like having another newborn, and there are SO many well behaved, already potty trained dogs just sitting in shelters waiting for a home. Since they're older, you'll already know what you're dealing with, no temperament or behavior surprises ESPECIALLY in a home with small children!

Dogs are a great addition to families and many breeds are very tolerant of children and prefer that setting.
I'm a part of a non-for-profit called Cause For Paws and I would be absolutely glad to help answer any questions you have about breeds, adoption, or breeder puppies. Please let me know! :)

comment_text: As a kid, I was one of those kids that needed everthing that would be offered .  I wore Salvation Army clothes 98 percent of the time. comment_text: That "Grass Bubble" is actually when rainwater or water in general can't properly go through the ground. You've got your layers of soil on the upper most part where grass it, then tiny little rocks and pebbles, and then finally big rocks way down. As water falls the ground naturally soaks it up and drains it, so you don't have puddles or muddy spots. However when there is too much water it clogs the layers up between the big rocks, and tiny little rocks and pebbles. That's how you get grass bubbles. Outrageous Acts of Science explains it better than I do.

The harness is definitely the safest way to ride! I'm glad you're doing that as long as possible. Just make sure those car seat mats either came with the car seat or was purchased from the manufacturer of the car seat. Otherwise, it's dangerous to have anything underneath the car seat. It should be just the car seat directly on top of the seat. And make sure you are attaching the top tether on all of those forward facing seats. It is literally what keeps the car seat in place during a collision and prevents your child from suffering a severe head injury. 

I've had extensive training in car seat safety. I'm always doing continuing education. I was watching some CPST videos on YouTube, and then YouTube recommended your carseat video. You seem like a fun group of people. I think I have another channel I have to follow. 🙂

comment_text:
I was in 5 point until I was 11, and I preferred it that way. My guardian tried switching me to a backless booster at 8 when she figured it was getting uncomfortable, and I hated it so she switched me back. Stayed comfy until 11, and within the seat limits. 

Another video of theirs is much more recent where the 12 year old twins are in 5 point and they were so outgrown of those seats. Even in the seats, feet were flat on the floor, harness was below their shoulders (and yep, forward facing obviously) so they weren’t even buckled correctly because they were way too big.

I’m all for 5 point harness as long as possible, but that long as possible stops when they reach the limits of the seat, which the twins did. That was the whole reason I unsubscribed from this family is because that video about the twins was spreading “it’s safest” while they were in fact, NOT in the safest seat for their size. Over the limits of the weight, especially weight, in a wreck the straps will break. That’s why there is a weight limit.

So to anyone seeing this in 2025 like me…yea, you’re subscribed to a family that risks their children’s safety by having kids in unsafe seats.

comment_text: SOCK PROBLEM SOLUTION: Have you heard of those net/mesh bags that you use for delicate clothes? They come in many different sizes, but you can get a couple bags for each of your kids (label the bags) and have them put all of their dirty socks throughout the week in the bag to be washed. It’s a lot less sorting to do and you know everybody gets their own socks back when they are clean because they are labeled. Obviously you don’t want to overfill each bag so get a couple.

video_title: TODDLER TRAUMATIZED AT DAYCARE!
comment_text: I am an infant/toddler teacher at a daycare center, so I've seen the crying more than a few times.  Here they are, being put in an unfamiliar place, with unfamiliar people, with out their comfort zone (mommy). My advice would to keep bringing him. If you stop bringing him, he will never learn to branch off from you or learn that it's okay for mommy to be gone, because I know she will be back. He needs to learn to trust others. He needs that social interaction with other kids and adults other than his immediate family. It's completely normal that he cried, and if you waited awhile and then bring him back, he'll still cry. Try to bring him as often as you can. Play there with him. Introduce him to the workers, talk to them while your holding him, try to let them hold him while you talk, then hold him again. -Might seem strange, but let Jackson see you hug them.- Stay a little while until he's comfortable enough that he can walk across the room to play with out bringing you with him. When he gets to the point of playing where he's not paying any attention, you can leave. Don't call his attention and say bye, just sneak away. Eventually, as he becomes more comfortable with the daycare, you'll have no problem with dropping him off.
